## Audio
Idle engine loop A (dist/assets/audio/engine-idle.wav): "Car engine loop 96kHz, 4s" by qubodup, OpenGameArt, CC-BY 3.0 (attribution: "Car engine loop by qubodup").
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/car-engine-loop-96khz-4s
License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 — https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/ (the page also lists GPL; this project uses the CC-BY option)
Processed: the 96 kHz 24-bit stereo recording (motor-loop-1.wav) downmixed to mono and resampled to 44.1 kHz. The loop point (3.93 s) is chosen by a search for matching wrap sample, slope and head/tail level (within 0.1 dB), so there is no crossfade. Measured −16.0 LUFS integrated, −5.5 dBFS peak. Its steady pitch is about 43.6 Hz. Pitch follows the rpm ratio over about 0.5 s; the level follows the rpm ratio over about 1.5 s. Level is 0.25 at idle and fades with cos(blend) from 1x to 5x the car's own idle, so it stays dominant of the recorded layers through the mid range. Pitch is clamped at 3x. Off-throttle it plays at 40% level.

High loop B (dist/assets/audio/engine-high.wav): "Engine-loop heavy vehicle/tank" (faster-speed copy "engine_heavy_fast_loop" from the heavy vehicle pack), by Nayckron, with collaborator qubodup, OpenGameArt, CC-BY 3.0 (attribution: "Engine-loop heavy vehicle/tank by Nayckron, with qubodup; modified from a car loop (source not named on the page)").
Source: https://opengameart.org/node/118761 (pack: https://opengameart.org/sites/default/files/engine-loop-heavy-pack_0.7z)
License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 — https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/ (the page also lists GPL 3.0; this project uses the CC-BY option)
Processed: the faster-speed WAV copy, mono, 44.1 kHz, cut at a loop point matched for slope and head/tail level (2.17 s, within 0.1 dB). Measured −16.0 LUFS integrated, −4.2 dBFS peak. It is a broadband heavy-engine rumble, not a harmonic engine. Its level is constant in rpm: a silent 0 at idle, rising smoothly (smoothstep) from 1.6x to 2.4x the car's own idle (the level ratio, about 1.5 s smoothing), and held at a ceiling of 0.1 before the off-throttle factor. Loop A stays louder through the mid range. Its rate is the pitch ratio (about 0.5 s smoothing) divided by 2.6 and capped at 0.7 to 1.3, so it is never pitched into a chipmunk. The 2.6 mapping and the 1.6x to 2.4x ramp are design choices, not verified by ear.

Boost whoosh (dist/assets/audio/boost-whoosh.wav): 0.9 s cut from "SFX: skid, countdown, boost, crash" (SuperTuxKart sound effects), by Scribe, OpenGameArt, CC0 1.0.
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/supertuxkart-sound-effects
License: CC0 1.0 — https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
The segment is identified from the pack listing and its position in the file, not by ear. Peak −3.0 dBFS.

Boost stinger (dist/assets/audio/boost-short.wav): "Boost or launch or thruster sound effect" by EZduzziteh, OpenGameArt, CC0 1.0.
Source: https://opengameart.org/content/boost-or-launch-or-thruster-sound-effect
License: CC0 1.0 — https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ . Peak −3.0 dBFS.

Impacts (dist/assets/audio/impact-heavy.mp3, impact-light.mp3): Kenney Impact Sounds, impactMetal_heavy_000 and impactGeneric_light_000 (re-encoded MP3, gain-trimmed to -3 dBFS peak).
Pickup clink (dist/assets/audio/pickup-clink.mp3): Kenney Impact Sounds, impactGlass_light_000 (re-encoded MP3). Trailing silence trimmed (about 0.11 s removed); peak about −2 dBFS after re-encode.
Pickup chime (dist/assets/audio/pickup-chime.mp3): Kenney Digital Audio, powerUp2 (re-encoded MP3). Silence trimmed at the start and end (ffmpeg silenceremove, −50 dB threshold) and a 3 ms fade-in baked in.
UI click (dist/assets/audio/ui-click.mp3): Kenney Interface Sounds, click_001 (re-encoded MP3). Trailing silence trimmed (about 0.06 s removed) and a 1 ms fade-in baked in (the transient peaks at about 1 ms, so a longer fade would remove it); peak about −2.8 dBFS after re-encode.
Source: https://kenney.nl/assets/impact-sounds, https://kenney.nl/assets/digital-audio, https://kenney.nl/assets/interface-sounds
License: CC0 1.0, Kenney (Creative Commons Zero) — https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

Removed in this update: dist/assets/audio/engine-loop.wav (0.72 s). It was the first 0.72 s of "racing car engine sound loops" by domasx2, OpenGameArt, CC0 1.0 (https://opengameart.org/content/racing-car-engine-sound-loops). The author states the source was a public-domain start-up sound, cut from https://pdsounds.org/sounds/start_up_car_with_seat_belt_warning_beep .

Synthesised in dist/audio.js (no third-party audio): the combustion engine voice (band-limited oscillators at the firing frequency, exhaust formant, grit shaper, gear-shift cut and clunk, lift pop, blow-off for turbo cars, rev-limiter cut), the electric inverter whine, tyre wobble and squeal, road rumble, wind and hiss, nitro whoosh, boost fallback sweep, traffic pass-by voices, and the generated reverb impulse response.

Reviewed but not shipped:
- "Engine sounds(2)" by pauliuw, OpenGameArt, CC0 1.0 (https://opengameart.org/node/4438). A 20 s revving recording whose pitch wanders between 25 and 130 Hz with weak periodicity, so there is no stable loop to cut.
- "Motor sound effect" by EZduzziteh, OpenGameArt, CC0 1.0 (https://opengameart.org/content/motor-sound-effect). A mouth-made 1 s motor loop, too short and too artificial.
- The other five "racing car engine sound loops" variants (domasx2, CC0). Pitch-shifted copies of one source.
- The base (slow-speed) heavy-vehicle loop and the slow and average copies of the same pack (Nayckron, CC-BY 3.0). Not used; the fast copy covers the upper revs.
- "Car engine start up" clips (looneybits, CC0; https://opengameart.org/node/93658 and https://opengameart.org/node/94039). Start-up sounds, not used.

## Garage collection additions (October 2026)

BMW E36 M3 by **Martin Trafas (TinoD2)**: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/bmw-e36-m3-762b90efd3dc413cb61c3e3c8097b8ac

Honda NSX 1990 by **Lexyc16**: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/honda-nsx-1990-1cc15628a00a4739a6b6c01128927c8d

Brutalist Interior garage by **vslite**: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/0eb40f2cb2bf4dfdbaae36095825788a

All three: **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0** — https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Optimized GLB redistributions: https://github.com/pedrosoandre/carros (geometry simplification/welding/pruning, Meshopt compression). Our runtime adaptations: BMW display plinth removed; vehicle rotation, centering and game scale; NSX wheel pivots recentered without changing geometry; garage staged with fill lights. Original materials retained. Names describe model subjects and do not imply manufacturer endorsement. Detailed primary-source verification and attribution accompany each GLB in assets/.

Meshopt decoder: official Three.js r170 distribution, MIT, bundled at vendor/libs/meshopt_decoder.module.js. https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/tree/r170

## Five-car collection and wheel rig update

Both Creative Commons Attribution 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Optimized licensed redistributions from https://github.com/pedrosoandre/carros (weld, simplification, prune, Meshopt compression). Adaptations: game scale/orientation, rebased authored wheel geometry, body paint choices, and wheel substitutions. GT alloy and Classic mesh options reuse wheel geometry from the credited Khronos Concept GT and Lexyc16 Honda NSX, respectively. Per-source attribution and primary verification records accompany the GLBs. All branding identifies subjects and does not imply endorsement.

## Knockable street furniture (assets/props/, see props-source.json)
"Rusty Fire Hydrant" by **tedpermana** — https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/rusty-fire-hydrant-4e0b0f865e7b4e6ebff58588dc8e769c — **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0** (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Shipped as assets/props/rusty-fire-hydrant.glb. Changes: simplified from 15k to ~1.9k triangles, textures downscaled to 512/256 px WebP, re-pivoted; runtime scale and sidewalk placement. No endorsement implied.
Metal Trash Can, Utility Box 01, Trashbag and Plastic Monobloc Chair 01 — **Poly Haven** (https://polyhaven.com/a/metal_trash_can, /a/utility_box_01, /a/trashbag, /a/plastic_monobloc_chair_01) — **CC0 1.0** (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). ## Pedestrians (assets/peds/, see peds-source.json)
Universal Base Characters [Standard] (Superhero_Male/Female_FullBody, Hair_SimpleParted, Hair_Buzzed, Hair_Beard, Hair_Long, Hair_Buns) and Universal Animation Library [Standard] (UAL1_Standard, in-place) by **Quaternius** — https://quaternius.com — **CC0 1.0** (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Shipped as assets/peds/ped-male.glb, ped-female.glb and ped-anims.glb. Changes: body, eyes, brows and hair merged into one skinned primitive per character (hair variants tagged by a _PART attribute), meshoptimizer-simplified to ~5k body triangles, skin base colour resized to 512 px WebP, normal/roughness maps dropped; 11 clips kept (rotations stored as normalized int16, pelvis translation only). Clothes are painted at runtime by a shader (dist/pedestrians.js), no extra textures.
